$comment: Risk-control → test binding manifest. Created as CAPA-001 action PA-1.
CAPA-001 root cause: 'The verification process accepts unexecuted,
unreproducible, self-attested prose as objective evidence for risk-control
implementation, and nothing in the build pipeline can contradict it.'
This file is the contradiction mechanism. Every risk control whose status is
'implemented' MUST name test node IDs that exist and pass. The manifest is
a named test has disappeared. Deleting a risk control's test therefore turns
CI red instead of producing a silent green build.
implemented  - control exists in code AND is bound to passing tests.
'tests' must be non-empty and every entry must resolve.
not_implemented - control does not exist. Recorded honestly. 'tests' empty.
deliberately_absent - the code intentionally does NOT provide this control;
unverified   - not yet re-verified to the CAPA-001 standard. Must not be
recorded as VERIFIED in the RMF until it is.

RC-006.description: AI-generated report carries a mandatory physician-review disclaimer
RC-006.negative_control: CAPA-001 §5.1 — enforcement line removed: 8 failed, 6 passed

RC-017.description: Authentication required on all API endpoints, including the WebSocket transport
RC-017.note: Covers authentication only. Object-level authorization is absent and is tracked as CAPA-002.

RC-007.description: De-identified data only sent to the third-party model API
RC-007.note: CAPA-001 §2.3 — no de-identification routine exists under backend/app/. Tracked as CAPA-001 CA-4. The RMF must not record this as VERIFIED.

RC-010.rationale: CAPA-001 §2.4 — the geometric classification path sets confidence = None on purpose, because it has no empirically calibrated confidence. Emitting an uncalibrated number would be worse than emitting none. The code is more honest than the documentation was; the RMF row is what must change, not the code.
RC-010.note: Requires a test asserting confidence stays None on the geometric path, so the deliberate absence cannot be 'fixed' by accident. Tracked under CA-3.

RC-022.description: All images preprocessed to MNI 1 mm isotropic space
RC-022.note: Superseded in effect by RC-024 (CAPA-001 CA-5). The MNI 1 mm claim remains unverified — recollection is not objective evidence — but the code no longer relies on it: voxel spacing is now required and validated rather than assumed. RC-022 itself should be retired or restated by the Safety Officer.

RC-001.description: All AI segmentation results labeled assistive / requires physician review
RC-001.note: RCV-2026-07-18 §3.3 — the phrase appears nowhere in the codebase; AI masks are indistinguishable from hand-drawn ones. Tracked as CAPA-001 CA-3.

RC-002.description: Viewing/Edit mode separation; AI results read-only until clinician activates edit
RC-002.implementation: frontend/src/components/ImageViewer2D.tsx (NOT ViewerApp.tsx as the RMF cites)
RC-002.note: Control is real and effective but not bound to a test; UI-layer only, no server-side enforcement. CA-3.

RC-003.description: Manual segmentation tools always available as override
RC-003.note: Rendered only when !is3D && activeSegmentation; in 3D there is no manual override. 'Always' is false. CA-3.

RC-004.description: Volumetry displays percentile ranges with normative reference
RC-004.note: Normative table has no provenance; sole call site omits patientAge so no percentile is ever computed. See CAPA-005.

RC-005.description: Abnormality flags show threshold criteria used
RC-005.note: Thresholds live only in Python comments; flag can never fire. See CAPA-005.

RC-008.description: Edge AI badge displays confidence and an unconditional assistive-only disclaimer
RC-008.implementation: frontend/src/components/QuickScreenBadge.tsx — disclaimer shares the result's visibility condition; no toggle
RC-008.negative_control: CAPA-004 CA-4.4 — toggle restored (showDisclaimer gate reinstated) → 2 failed, 3 passed
RC-008.note: Repaired under CAPA-004 CA-4.4. Previously the string existed in the component but was gated behind useState(false), so a user could read a confidence-scored verdict with no limitation statement — while the file's header comment claimed it was always shown. Verification by grepping for the string could not tell a displayed control from a hidden one.

RC-009.description: Edge AI model admin-supplied; feature hidden when unavailable
RC-009.note: Verified by inspection 2026-07-18 and broader than claimed (also rejects text/html), but not bound to a test. ID conflicts with the withdrawn RCV-SUMMARY. CA-3.

RC-011.note: Displayed and honest, but the control names EDT/Atlas/Geometric while the UI exposes auto/msmask/geometric. Wording cannot be mapped to the screen. CA-3.

RC-012.note: Purely dimensional; a no-op on square 256x256 volumes, the standard brain-MRI matrix. See CAPA-004 CA-4.3.

RC-013.note: No orientation validation on upload. CAPA-004 CA-4.1 has landed the primitives (see RC-023) but they are NOT yet wired into load_nifti_from_bytes — see RC-023's note for why that migration must convert image and mask together. Also outstanding: L/R laterality labels on the viewport (CA-4.2). See CAPA-004.

RC-014.note: Implemented exactly as written — the only control of which that is true — but not bound to a test. CA-3.

RC-015.description: DIS per-region details with qualifying lesion counts
RC-015.note: 3 of 5 McDonald 2024 regions, correctly and honestly disclosed. Counts are returned and typed but rendered by no component. CA-3.

RC-016.description: Patient name and MRN rendered in the image viewport itself
RC-016.negative_control: CAPA-004 CA-4.2 — three vectors: identity block removed → 1 failed; overlay unwired from ImageViewer2D → 1 failed; orientation warning silenced → 2 failed
RC-016.note: Covers the 2D viewer. 3D and multi-panel views still receive no patient props and remain uncovered — tracked under CAPA-004 CA-4.2. Tests assert what is RENDERED, not what is passed: the original defect was a dead prop that looked correct at the call site.

RC-018.note: Model correct; 7 of 124 routes enforce a permission, 0 enforce a role, 10 of 15 permissions never checked. See CAPA-004 CA-4.5 and CAPA-002.

RC-019.description: DICOM-SEG with standard SOP Class UID
RC-019.note: Code correct. Tests exist but are not RC-named, so the manifest gate cannot bind them yet; the RMF claimed 8 tests and there are 7. CA-3.

RC-020.description: DICOMweb import shows metadata before import
RC-020.note: Source metadata is shown, but the destination is an unvalidated free-text prompt() patient ID with no name confirmation — a mis-association hazard covered by no control. CA-3.

RC-021.description: Report generation timeout (30s) with error message
RC-021.note: No timeout exists anywhere in the report path; no CLAUDE_TIMEOUT setting. Also a synchronous call inside an async handler blocks the worker. CA-3.

RC-023.description: Anatomical orientation is determinable from the affine, and is never guessed when indeterminate
RC-023.negative_control: CAPA-004 CA-4.1 — fixed RAS return → 9 failed; canonicalisation neutralised → 2 failed. CA-4.2 — orientation warning silenced in the viewport → 2 failed
RC-023.note: NEW control created by CAPA-004 CA-4.1; MUST be added to the Risk Management File §5.1 (tracked). It provides the primitives only. RC-013 — orientation VALIDATION ON UPLOAD — remains not_implemented because canonicalisation is deliberately opt-in: image and mask load through separate calls, so transforming one and not the other would misalign them and create a worse hazard than the one being fixed. Migrating to canonical-by-default must convert both together in one change, with a matched-pair correspondence test. The viewport now REPORTS the orientation and warns when it is UNKNOWN or non-canonical, but deliberately renders NO L/R edge labels: volumes are not canonicalised on load and imaging_service transposes with fixed axis tuples presuming RAS, so the axis-to-screen mapping is unverified. A test asserts that absence. Labels may only be added under CA-4.3, after verification against a phantom of known laterality.

RC-024.description: Voxel spacing is required for every quantitative measurement; never assumed
RC-024.implementation: backend/app/utils/spacing_utils.py::resolve_voxel_spacing / require_spacing; 4 route sites and 14 Class C service signatures
RC-024.negative_control: CAPA-001 CA-5 — helper returns 1mm default → 17 failed; a route restores the default → 1 failed
RC-024.note: Supersedes the RC-022 assumption that all images are MNI 1 mm, which was 'verified by recollection'. The code no longer depends on that assumption: it requires the real geometry and raises (HTTP 422, VOXEL_SPACING_UNAVAILABLE) when it is unavailable.

RC-025.description: Role-level authorization enforced on every patient-record route
RC-025.implementation: app/security/models.py (4 PATIENT_* permissions), app/security/rbac.py (role map), app/api/routes/patients.py (10/10 routes)
RC-025.negative_control: CAPA-004 CA-4.5 — three vectors: a route reverted to authentication-only → 3 failed; VIEWER granted PATIENT_DELETE → 4 failed; created_by capture removed → 1 failed
RC-025.note: SCOPE LIMIT: answers 'may this ROLE operate on patient records', NOT 'may this user access THIS patient'. Object-level authorization remains absent and CAPA-002 CA-2.1 stays OPEN — an authenticated VIEWER still reaches every patient in the system. Do not read this control as closing CAPA-002. Ten route docstrings previously promised PATIENT_* permissions that did not exist in the enum and were enforced nowhere.

RC-026.description: Object-level authorization for patient records under the care-team entitlement model
RC-026.implementation: app/security/patient_access.py (pure decision) + app/services/care_team_service.py (assignment store) + app/security/patient_access_dependency.py (HTTP guard) + app/api/routes/patients.py (6 patient-scoped routes + care-team management)
RC-026.negative_control: decision layer — 4 vectors (7/2/1/7 failed); enforcement layer — 3 vectors: guard removed from a route -> 1 failed; enforcement returns patient unconditionally -> 7 failed; 403 instead of 404 (enumeration leak) -> 1 failed
RC-026.note: ENFORCED on the PATIENT resource: all 6 patient-scoped routes (get/update/delete + 3 medical-history) plus care-team management now call require_patient_access, which denies with 404 (never 403) to prevent patient enumeration. Care-team assignment/revocation themselves require object access, so a clinician cannot add themselves to a team they are not on; ADMIN bootstraps. STILL OPEN under CAPA-002: imaging.py, studies.py and documents.py are NOT yet wired — they identify the patient indirectly (via file_id / study_id), which needs CA-2.3 (opaque IDs resolved server-side) first. CAPA-002 remains OPEN until those routes enforce access and CA-2.3 lands.

RC-027.description: Imaging storage references are parsed against a positive grammar and patient-authorized; raw client paths are never used as bucket keys
RC-027.implementation: app/security/storage_access.py::parse_patient_storage_ref (pure grammar) + app/security/patient_access_dependency.py::authorize_storage_ref (parse + RC-026) + app/api/routes/imaging.py (8 handlers authorize before any storage access)
RC-027.negative_control: 3 vectors, each re-measured in isolation after a chained run gave a spurious result: prefix check removed -> 1 failed; UUID validation skipped -> 2 failed; object_path echoes raw input -> 2 failed
RC-027.note: Closes the imaging half of CAPA-002. Malformed references and cross-patient references both return an identical 404 (no enumeration oracle over key space or patient space). object_path is rebuilt from parsed components, so no unparsed caller byte reaches the storage key. SCOPE: patient-scoped imaging grammar only. Segmentation objects (segmentations/{id}/...) and the studies/documents routes are NOT yet covered — CAPA-002 remains OPEN for those.
